definition: Ardor means burning intensity of feeling — heat that keeps its flame through setbacks.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word ardor. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know ardor should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: No string of rained-out weekends could dampen the kite club president's ardor for flying.
Enthusiasm is bright and real, but it is a milder flame than ardor — it can cool after one bad season.
Obsession goes further than ardor — ardor burns hot but leaves you whole; obsession crowds everything else out of the room.

Passion is the broad, everyday word for strong feeling of any kind — for a person, a craft, a cause. Ardor is passion at a particular temperature: heat that keeps burning through obstacles. Like ardor, passion can coexist with a full life; neither word says the feeling has crowded everything else aside.

Zeal is a compliment: it praises tireless, sleeves-rolled-up energy spent in service of something worthwhile — a cause, a mission, a campaign. Ardor names the heat of the feeling itself, whether or not it is doing any work that day. Zeal is measured in effort; ardor is measured in temperature.
